name: Chichen Itza (El Castillo)
description: Astronomically aligned stepped pyramid of Kukulcan in Yucatán, an official New 7 Wonder of the World.
history: Major ceremonial city and political capital of the Terminal Classic Maya civilization, integrating Maya mathematics, geometry, and Toltec architectural artistry.
construction: Built of limestone masonry featuring 365 total steps (equaling days in the solar year), four 91-step staircases plus the top platform.
architecture: During the spring and autumn equinoxes, the setting sun casts a shadow across the pyramid that resembles a feathered serpent (Kukulcan) slithering down the balustrade.
significance: Designated an official New 7 Wonder of the World on July 7, 2007 and UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1988.
currentStatus: Standing and actively conserved in Yucatán, Mexico.
wonderHistoricalContext: Voted onto the official New 7 Wonders of the World roster on July 7, 2007, celebrated for its astronomical precision and Mesoamerican sacred geometry.
